land.text: the whole of Iran: 'by October 1925 the Majlis agreed to depose and formally exile Ahmad Shah Qajar'; 'The Majlis declared Reza Pahlavi as the Shah of Iran on 12 December 1925'

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Pahlavi row starts in 1924 and its Qajar row stops in 1923; the qajar-dynasty dossier carries 1924 to October 1925 on a new keyframe, so this dossier starts in December 1925.

land.text: Iran as the last Pahlavi shape drew it: the Pahlavi dynasty was deposed on 11 February 1979 and the monarchy abolished and a republic declared

successors.note: Cliopatria ends this row in 1978 and starts the Islamic Republic of Iran in 1979 on the same outline; that dossier dates the republic to April 1979.

capitals.name: Tehran
capitals.note: The Reza Shah page has Reza Khan 'marched towards Tehran and seized the capital' in February 1921; no page opened lists a later capital.

rulers.name: Reza Shah Pahlavi
rulers.note: 15 December 1925 to 16 September 1941 (abdicated). The Majlis declared him Shah on 12 December 1925; the Reza Shah page has the abdication on 16 September 1941 in one place and 17 September in another.

correction.text: years only: the shape holds from the Majlis vote of 12 December 1925; 1924 to October 1925 is Qajar Iran under Prime Minister Reza Khan (the qajar-dynasty dossier's new keyframe qajar-dynasty_1924)

keyframe_review.note: 1924-1925 in Cliopatria, 1,624,335 km2: all of Iran. The page: 'Founded: 15 December 1925' and 'Preceded by House of Qajar'. The pages opened give no infobox area, so no ratio could be taken. Reza Khan had been prime minister since October 1923 and restored central authority in Khuzestan in late 1924 (Reza Shah page); neither moves the outline.

1926-1931, same outline. The Reza Shah page lists the Simko Shikak revolt (1926) and the 'Persian conquest of West Baluchistan (1928-1935)' in its infobox without detail; Cliopatria already draws Baluchistan inside Iran.
1932-1935, 1,624,310 km2: one Iraqi cell (250 km2) fewer than 1926, read as noise. No page opened dates a frontier change in these years.

1936-1941, 1,624,037 km2: the frontier Iran enters the war with. About 30 cells (7,500 km2) lie in Afghanistan, Pakistan, Iraq and Turkmenistan against Natural Earth, an edge effect of the old frontier lines. The Anglo-Soviet invasion began on 25 August 1941.

correction.text: the full 1936 outline of Iran, 1,624,037 km2: the cut-out of about 1,840 cells (460,000 km2) is Allied-occupied Iranian land, not British or Soviet land, and is drawn by the occupation events

keyframe_review.note: 1942-1945, 1,158,493 km2 in Cliopatria, 465,000 km2 less than 1936. The cut-out is exactly the British Colonial Empire shape's 1,161 cells inside Iran (Khuzestan, Lorestan, Kermanshah, Hamadan, Ilam, Kordestan) and the Soviet Union shape's 675 cells (Azerbaijan, Gilan, Mazandaran, the north). The page: 'Military occupation of Iran for the remainder of World War II', 'the Soviets stationed in northern Iran and the British south of Hamadan and Qazvin', and 'The Allies withdrew from Tehran on 17 October' 1941. Iran stayed sovereign, so the shape is the full outline and the zones are occupations (rule 4).

correction.text: the full 1936 outline of Iran: the British zone was handed back (Cliopatria 1946 already has it) and the Soviet zone, Azerbaijan People's Government and Mahabad Republic are drawn by events until December 1946

keyframe_review.note: 1946, 1,447,946 km2 in Cliopatria: the British zone is back, the 677 northern cells (Azerbaijan, Gilan, Mazandaran, Golestan, Zanjan, Kordestan) are still Soviet in Cliopatria's Soviet 1946 shape. The page: Soviet troops 'left as of May 6' 1946, while the 'Azerbaijan People's Government' and the Mahabad Republic held the north-west until 'Iranian troops entered the region in December 1946'. Iran never ceased to be sovereign there, so the full outline is the shape and the rebels and the occupation are events.

1947-1975, 1,624,310 km2, the full outline restored after the Iranian army entered Azerbaijan and Mahabad in December 1946. Unchanged for 29 years: no page opened dates a frontier change except the Tunbs and Abu Musa in 1971, which are smaller than one 250 km2 cell and are not in the grid.
1976-1978, same outline as 1947; the Pahlavi page gives no area and no territorial event in these years.

correction.text: years only: the 1978 shape carried to 11 February 1979, when the dynasty was deposed

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria ends this row in 1978 but the page gives 'Deposition: 11 February 1979'. The Islamic Republic of Iran dossier starts in April 1979 on the same outline and may duplicate the year.

region.text: all of Iran: the Majlis 'declared Reza Pahlavi as the Shah of Iran'

ledger.note: December 1925: Reza Khan becomes Shah and founds the Pahlavi dynasty. 'The Majlis declared Reza Pahlavi as the Shah of Iran on 12 December 1925' (infobox 'Founded: 15 December 1925'); Ahmad Shah Qajar had been deposed in October 1925. Reza Khan had been prime minister since October 1923. The page names no land, so the whole of Iran is the researcher's reading.

region.text: West Baluchistan, 'Baluchi khans such as Bahram Khan and Dost Mohammad Khan controlled the southeast': the province of Sistan and Baluchestan without the Sistan region

ledger.note: 1928: the Persian conquest of West Baluchistan begins. The Reza Shah page lists 'Persian conquest of West Baluchistan (1928-1935)' in its infobox and says only that 'Baluchi khans such as Bahram Khan and Dost Mohammad Khan controlled the southeast'. The Baluchestan land is already inside Cliopatria's Pahlavi shape for 1924-1946 and the page names no frontier and no gain, so this is an internal pacification drawn as a contested zone, not an acquisition (the earlier 1935 gain was dropped after review); the years are the infobox's, the region is the researcher's reading.

region.text: West Baluchistan, 'Baluchi khans such as Bahram Khan and Dost Mohammad Khan controlled the southeast': the province of Sistan and Baluchestan without the Sistan region

ledger.note: 1935: the conquest of West Baluchistan ends. The page gives only the infobox span '(1928-1935)' and no battle or treaty; the khans' land stays Iranian in every Cliopatria shape, so nothing changes hands.

region.text: the Soviet zone: 'the Soviets stationed in northern Iran' (Iranian Azerbaijan with Tabriz and Ardabil, Gilan, Mazandaran, Khorasan, Qazvin), drawn as the part of Cliopatria's Soviet 1942 shape that lies inside Iran

ledger.note: 25 August 1941: the Soviet Union invades northern Iran. 'with fighting beginning on 25 August'; 'by 26 August, occupied all of Iranian Azerbaijan (including Tabriz and Ardabil)'; the Gilan attack began on 25 August. The zone is the researcher's reading of the page's provinces.

region.text: the British zone: 'the British south of Hamadan and Qazvin' (Abadan, Khorramshahr, Bandar Shahpur, Ahvaz, Qasr-e Shirin, Kermanshah), drawn as the part of Cliopatria's British Colonial Empire 1942 shape that lies inside Iran

ledger.note: 25 August 1941: British and Indian forces invade the south. Abadan and Khorramshahr were captured on the first day, Ahvaz 'by the early morning of 27 August', Qasr-e Shirin was broken through, Kermanshah entered 'on 1 September'.

region.text: the Soviet zone: 'the Soviets stationed in northern Iran' (Iranian Azerbaijan with Tabriz and Ardabil, Gilan, Mazandaran, Khorasan, Qazvin), drawn as the part of Cliopatria's Soviet 1942 shape that lies inside Iran

ledger.note: 31 August 1941: the fighting ends. 'the Shah ordered his military to stop fighting and stand down on 29 August', a ceasefire was agreed on 30 August and 'fighting ... ending on 31 August'.

region.text: the British zone: 'the British south of Hamadan and Qazvin' (Abadan, Khorramshahr, Bandar Shahpur, Ahvaz, Qasr-e Shirin, Kermanshah), drawn as the part of Cliopatria's British Colonial Empire 1942 shape that lies inside Iran

ledger.note: 31 August 1941: the fighting ends in the south (stand-down 29 August, ceasefire 30 August).

region.text: the Soviet zone: 'the Soviets stationed in northern Iran' (Iranian Azerbaijan with Tabriz and Ardabil, Gilan, Mazandaran, Khorasan, Qazvin), drawn as the part of Cliopatria's Soviet 1942 shape that lies inside Iran

ledger.note: September 1941: the Soviets hold the north. Infobox 'Military occupation of Iran for the remainder of World War II'; 'the Soviets stationed in northern Iran'; the Red Army entered Tehran on 17 September and 'the Allies withdrew from Tehran on 17 October', so the capital is left out of the zones. Reza Shah abdicated on 16 September.

region.text: the British zone: 'the British south of Hamadan and Qazvin' (Abadan, Khorramshahr, Bandar Shahpur, Ahvaz, Qasr-e Shirin, Kermanshah), drawn as the part of Cliopatria's British Colonial Empire 1942 shape that lies inside Iran

ledger.note: September 1941: the British hold the south, 'south of Hamadan and Qazvin'. The Tripartite Treaty of Alliance (29 January 1942) promised withdrawal 'not more than six months after the cessation of hostilities'.

region.text: Iranian Azerbaijan under Sayyid Jafar Pishevari's Azerbaijan People's Government (the page names no boundary; Azerbaijan minus the Mahabad area)

ledger.note: November 1945: the Azerbaijan People's Government takes Iranian Azerbaijan. Its page gives 'Established: 20 November 1945' and says the militia 'started a bloodless coup on 18 November 1945' and 'by 21 November they had captured all remaining government posts in the province'; the Iran crisis page's 'by mid-December 1945' dates the second pro-Soviet republic (Mahabad), not this one. The page names no boundary, so the region (Azerbaijan minus the Mahabad area) is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the Mahabad Republic, 'proclaimed in December 1945' (the page names no boundary; a radius around Mahabad)

ledger.note: December 1945: the Kurdish Mahabad Republic. 'The Mahabad Republic was proclaimed in December 1945'; 'Qazi Muhammad was elected the first president on January 22, 1946'. The page names no boundary.

region.text: the British zone: 'the British south of Hamadan and Qazvin' (Abadan, Khorramshahr, Bandar Shahpur, Ahvaz, Qasr-e Shirin, Kermanshah), drawn as the part of Cliopatria's British Colonial Empire 1942 shape that lies inside Iran

ledger.note: March 1946: the British leave. The page has the British begin to withdraw 'when the deadline for withdrawal arrived on 2 March 1946'; it gives no date for the last British soldier.

region.text: the Soviet zone: 'the Soviets stationed in northern Iran' (Iranian Azerbaijan with Tabriz and Ardabil, Gilan, Mazandaran, Khorasan, Qazvin), drawn as the part of Cliopatria's Soviet 1942 shape that lies inside Iran

ledger.note: 6 May 1946: the Soviets leave Iran. Stalin 'ordered the withdrawal of Soviet troops from Iran by April 30, 1946' after the 2 March deadline had been violated; 'The Soviet troops left as of May 6.' The Anglo-Soviet invasion page says 'May 1946'.

region.text: Iranian Azerbaijan under Sayyid Jafar Pishevari's Azerbaijan People's Government (the page names no boundary; Azerbaijan minus the Mahabad area)

ledger.note: December 1946: the army retakes Azerbaijan. 'Iranian troops entered the region in December 1946'; result 'Iranian victory' and 'Dissolution of the Azerbaijan People's Government and the Republic of Mahabad'.

region.text: the Mahabad Republic, 'proclaimed in December 1945' (the page names no boundary; a radius around Mahabad)

ledger.note: 15 December 1946: the Kurdish republic falls. 'The Barzanis ... withdrew to Naqada on December 15, 1946' and the Iranian military then entered Mahabad.

region.text: the Tunb Islands and Abu Musa in the Persian Gulf (Abu Musa under joint administration with Sharjah)

ledger.note: 30 November 1971: Iran seizes the Tunbs and Abu Musa. 'On 30 November 1971, Iran forcibly seized control of the Tunb Islands and Abu Musa', a day after the 29 November agreement of joint administration of Abu Musa with Sharjah, 'shortly before the end of the British protectorate and the formation of the UAE'. The islands (10.3 and 2 km2 for the Tunbs, 12.8 km2 for Abu Musa) are smaller than a map cell; they come from Ras al-Khaimah and Sharjah. The region is now three circles at the coordinates the Tunbs and Abu Musa pages print (they still resolve to no cells until the gazetteer has the island names). The Abu Musa page dates the Iran-Sharjah memorandum of understanding to 30 November 1971.

region.text: Iran: the dynasty's 'Deposition: 11 February 1979'; 'Monarchy abolished Republic declared'

ledger.note: 11 February 1979: the Pahlavi dynasty falls. Infobox 'Deposition: 11 February 1979', the succession table 'Monarchy abolished Republic declared'; the page has the dynasty 'removed from power in 1979'.

wars.outcome: Listed in the Reza Shah infobox without description; no border moved.

zones.text: West Baluchistan, 'Baluchi khans such as Bahram Khan and Dost Mohammad Khan controlled the southeast': the province of Sistan and Baluchestan without the Sistan region

wars.outcome: The Baluch khans who 'controlled the southeast' after the 1921 coup were brought under the Shah's rule by 1935; no frontier moved.
wars.note: The page gives only the infobox entry '(1928-1935)'; the dates are the page's, the description and the zone are the researcher's reading (re-read 2026-10-25: the page has no other sentence on the conquest and does not mention Sistan). Recorded as contest_start 1928 / contest_end 1935, not as a gain.

wars.name: Anglo-Soviet invasion of Iran

zones.text: the Soviet zone: 'the Soviets stationed in northern Iran' (Iranian Azerbaijan with Tabriz and Ardabil, Gilan, Mazandaran, Khorasan, Qazvin), drawn as the part of Cliopatria's Soviet 1942 shape that lies inside Iran

the British zone: 'the British south of Hamadan and Qazvin' (Abadan, Khorramshahr, Bandar Shahpur, Ahvaz, Qasr-e Shirin, Kermanshah), drawn as the part of Cliopatria's British Colonial Empire 1942 shape that lies inside Iran

wars.outcome: Anglo-Soviet victory in six days (25-31 August 1941): Reza Shah abdicated on 16 September in favour of Mohammad Reza and the north (Soviet) and south (British) were occupied for the remainder of the war.

wars.name: Iran crisis of 1946

zones.text: Iranian Azerbaijan under Sayyid Jafar Pishevari's Azerbaijan People's Government (the page names no boundary; Azerbaijan minus the Mahabad area)
the Mahabad Republic, 'proclaimed in December 1945' (the page names no boundary; a radius around Mahabad)

wars.outcome: Iranian victory: the Soviets left on 6 May 1946 and Iranian troops entered Azerbaijan and Mahabad in December 1946, dissolving both republics.

wars.name: Iranian seizure of the Tunbs and Abu Musa

zones.text: Greater Tunb, Lesser Tunb and Abu Musa

wars.outcome: Iran took the Tunbs and half-administered Abu Musa on 30 November 1971; the UAE still disputes it.

certainty.note: The tribal periphery was not under central control: Khuzestan until late 1924, West Baluchistan until 1935, Kurdish and Turkmen marches; the frontiers are those the Qajar state left.
Cliopatria holds a single outline of 1.62 M km2; the frontiers are the treaty lines inherited from the Qajar dossier. No page opened here describes a survey or dates a frontier change.
The Allied zones of 1941-46 follow provinces and the line 'south of Hamadan and Qazvin'; the rebel republics' boundaries are not given by the page.
The land frontiers are unchanged; the 1971 Gulf islands are smaller than a map cell and their sovereignty is still disputed by the UAE.

notes:
Qajar to Pahlavi is a change of dynasty on the same land (rule 2) but Cliopatria keeps two rows and the group split the dossiers: qajar-dynasty ends October 1925 (new keyframe for 1924-25) and this dossier starts in December 1925, so the colour agent may want one colour for both; the Islamic Republic starts in April 1979 on the same outline.

Start and end: Cliopatria 1924..1978; the pages give 12 December 1925 (Majlis vote) or 15 December 1925 (infobox) and 11 February 1979. Added keyframes: pahlavi-dynasty_1979 (1979 only). The 1942 and 1946 Cliopatria shapes are wrong for a sovereign state: they are the full outline minus the Allied zones that Cliopatria draws as British Colonial Empire (1,161 cells, 1942-1945) and as the Soviet Union (675 cells, 1942-1946); the same Soviet shape keeps northern Iran through 1946 although the Soviets left on 6 May 1946 (a flag for the eu-17 dossier). The occupation events are recorded from the owner's side with the occupier as counterpart.

Rebel counterparts azerbaijan-people-s-government (20 November 1945 to December 1946) and republic-of-mahabad (December 1945 to December 1946) were written by this batch (me-10-h). Counterparts used by string: Baluch khans of West Baluchistan (contest 1928-1935 only; the 1935 'gain' of Sistan and Baluchestan was removed after review because the 1924, 1926 and 1932 shapes and the founding region already hold the province and the Reza Shah page names no gain, only the infobox span 'Persian conquest of West Baluchistan (1928-1935)'). The Sheikh Khazal rebellion (late 1924) was removed from wars: it falls in qajar-dynasty's years (to October 1925). Gazetteer names needed: Greater Tunb (26°15′N 55°16′E), Lesser Tunb (26°14′N 55°08′E) and Abu Musa (25°52′N 55°02′E), the coordinates the pages print; the islands are not grid cells, so the 1971 gain (now three 15 km circles) still resolves to no cells. The loss to the Azerbaijan People's Government is dated 1945-11 (its page) and the Mahabad loss 1945-12.

Not reached in the five-page budget: the Bahrain claim (dropped 1970), the 1975 Algiers Agreement and the 1937 Shatt al-Arab treaty with Iraq, the 1932-1937 Turkish frontier settlement and the 1935 Helmand dispute (the Reza Shah page covers none of them), the Republic of Gilan's aftermath (the qajar-dynasty dossier has it), and Mossadegh's 1953 fall (no border). The pages give no infobox area, so Cliopatria's 1,624,335 km2 could not be compared.
